description: distillation tasks with the independent Python program's stdout as expected output

tasks.title: Warehouse Pallet Stacking
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse stacks pallets in a column. A column may hold at most 5 pallets. Pallets come in three weights: light (10 kg), medium (20 kg), heavy (30 kg). The column must never exceed a total weight of 60 kg.

Count the number of distinct sequences of pallets (each position holds one pallet type or is left empty) such that:
- The column has at most 5 positions.
- The sum of weights of occupied positions is at most 60.
- Positions are filled from the bottom; once a position is empty, all positions above it must also be empty (no gaps).

Output exactly 4 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Max pallets: 5
Weight limit: 60
Valid stacks: <count>
With at most 3 pallets: <count of valid stacks using 0, 1, 2, or 3 pallets>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Max pallets: 5
Weight limit: 60
Valid stacks: 51
With at most 3 pallets: 30
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Beekeeper Honey Jar Filling
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper fills honey jars of capacity 7 units. Honey is available in portions of sizes 1, 3, and 5 units. Portions may be used any number of times, and the order of portions matters (pouring 1 then 3 is different from 3 then 1).

Count the number of sequences of portions whose total is exactly 7.

Output exactly 4 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Jar capacity: 7
Portion sizes: 1 3 5
Sequences: <count>
Sequences using at most 4 portions: <count of sequences of length 1, 2, 3, or 4>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Jar capacity: 7
Portion sizes: 1 3 5
Sequences: 12
Sequences using at most 4 portions: 6
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Library Bookshelf Arrangement
tasks.prompt:
A library arranges books on a shelf of 6 slots. Books come in three heights: short (S), medium (M), tall (T). For visual balance, a tall book may not be placed directly next to another tall book, and the shelf must not have more than 3 tall books total.

Count the number of arrangements of 6 slots, each holding one of S, M, or T, satisfying both rules.

Output exactly 5 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Slots: 6
Valid arrangements: <count>
With 0 tall books: <count>
With 1 or 2 tall books: <count>
With exactly 3 tall books: <count>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Slots: 6
Valid arrangements: 448
With 0 tall books: 64
With 1 or 2 tall books: 352
With exactly 3 tall books: 32
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Farm Fence Post Painting
tasks.prompt:
A farmer paints a fence made of 7 posts in a row. Each post is painted red (R), white (W), or blue (B). For decoration, no two adjacent posts may share the same color, and the first and last posts must also differ in color (the fence forms a visual loop even though it is a line).

Count the number of valid colorings of the 7 posts.

Output exactly 4 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Posts: 7
Colors: R W B
Valid colorings: <count>
Colorings where post 1 is R: <count>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Posts: 7
Colors: R W B
Valid colorings: 126
Colorings where post 1 is R: 42
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Kitchen Spice Rack Combinations
tasks.prompt:
A cook arranges a spice rack with 5 shelves. Each shelf holds one of three spice jars: salt (S), pepper (P), or garlic (G). For safety, a shelf holding pepper (P) may not be directly above or below another shelf holding pepper.

Count the number of valid arrangements of the 5 shelves.

Output exactly 4 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Shelves: 5
Spices: S P G
Valid arrangements: <count>
Arrangements with no pepper at all: <count>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Shelves: 5
Spices: S P G
Valid arrangements: 164
Arrangements with no pepper at all: 32
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Bakery Tray Layout Planner
tasks.prompt:
A bakery lays out a rectangular tray of 3 rows and 4 columns. Each cell holds either a croissant (C) or is left empty (.). For quality control, no row may contain more than 2 croissants, and no column may contain more than 2 croissants.

Count the number of valid tray layouts.

Output exactly 5 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Rows: 3
Columns: 4
Valid layouts: <count>
Layouts with exactly 4 croissants: <count>
Layouts with 6 or more croissants: <count>
tasks.expected_stdout:
Rows: 3
Columns: 4
Valid layouts: 1081
Layouts with exactly 4 croissants: 360
Layouts with 6 or more croissants: 114
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Train Platform Signal Simulation
tasks.prompt:
A small train station has a 5x5 grid of signal lights. Each cell is either 'on' or 'off'. The initial state of the grid is given below (rows top to bottom, columns left to right):

Row 0: on, off, on, off, on
Row 1: off, on, on, off, off
Row 2: on, off, off, on, off
Row 3: off, off, on, on, on
Row 4: on, on, off, off, on

The station runs a signal refresh cycle. For each cell, count how many of its 8 neighbours (orthogonal and diagonal) are 'on'. A cell becomes 'on' in the next state if it currently has at least 3 'on' neighbours; otherwise it becomes 'off'. Corners and edges only count the neighbours that exist on the grid.

After ONE refresh cycle, output the result. Print exactly 5 lines, one per row from top to bottom. In each line print 5 characters '1' for on and '0' for off with no spaces between them.

Print one final line containing the total number of 'on' cells after the refresh in the exact format:
Total: N
where N is an integer.
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Garden Drip Irrigation Coverage
tasks.prompt:
A rectangular garden is represented as a 6x6 grid of square plots. Each plot has a water demand value (an integer). The demands are given as a 6x6 table:

Row 0: 3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9
Row 1: 2, 6, 5, 3, 5, 8
Row 2: 9, 7, 9, 3, 2, 3
Row 3: 8, 4, 6, 2, 6, 4
Row 4: 3, 5, 8, 9, 7, 9
Row 5: 3, 2, 3, 8, 4, 6

A single drip sprinkler head is placed at row 2, column 3 (0-indexed). The sprinkler waters a square region of radius 1 around its position: it waters the cell itself plus every cell whose row differs by at most 1 and whose column differs by at most 1 (so up to 3x3 cells), clipped to the grid bounds.

Output exactly 3 lines in this exact format:
Region sum: S
Region average: A.A
High demand cells: H

Where S is the sum of the demand values of all watered cells, A.A is the average demand of those cells rounded to 1 decimal place, and H is the count of watered cells whose demand is at least 6.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Region sum: 41
Region average: 4.6
High demand cells: 3
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Board Game Tile Scoring
tasks.prompt:
A board game uses a 5x5 grid of tiles. Each tile shows a number 0-4. The grid is:

Row 0: 1, 2, 1, 0, 3
Row 1: 0, 1, 2, 1, 0
Row 2: 3, 0, 4, 0, 2
Row 3: 0, 1, 0, 1, 1
Row 4: 2, 0, 3, 0, 4

A player places a token at row 2, column 2. The score is computed by expanding outward one ring at a time. Ring 0 is just the token cell. Ring 1 is all cells whose Chebyshev distance from the token is exactly 1. Ring 2 is all cells whose Chebyshev distance is exactly 2. Continue until the ring would fall outside the grid.

For each ring that has at least one cell on the grid, output one line in this exact format:
Ring R: sum S, count C

where R is the ring number starting from 0, S is the sum of tile values in that ring, and C is the number of cells in that ring.

Finally output one line:
Total score: T
where T is the sum of all ring sums.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Ring 0: sum 4, count 1
Ring 1: sum 6, count 8
Ring 2: sum 22, count 16
Total score: 32
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Robot Warehouse Cleaning Path
tasks.prompt:
A cleaning robot moves on a 7x7 grid of floor tiles. Each tile is either dirty (D) or clean (C). The initial floor is:

Row 0: D, D, C, D, C, C, D
Row 1: C, D, C, C, D, C, C
Row 2: D, C, D, D, C, D, C
Row 3: C, C, C, D, C, C, D
Row 4: D, D, C, C, D, C, C
Row 5: C, D, D, C, C, D, D
Row 6: D, C, C, D, C, C, D

The robot starts at row 0, column 0. It follows this fixed plan: repeat 6 times, each iteration move one step to the right (increasing column), then one step down (increasing row). If a move would go past the last column or last row, the robot stays in place for that move. After each move (including a stay), the robot cleans the tile it is on, changing D to C.

After the full plan, output:
1. Exactly 7 lines showing the final floor grid. Each line is 7 characters with no spaces, using 'D' for dirty and 'C' for clean.
2. One line: Robot final position: r, c  (with r and c being integers, no spaces after the colon before the number, one space after the comma)
3. One line: Dirty remaining: N  (N is an integer count of D cells left)
tasks.expected_stdout:
CCCDCCD
CCCCDCC
DCCCCDC
CCCCCCD
DDCCCCC
CDDCCCC
DCCDCCC
Robot final position: 6, 6
Dirty remaining: 12
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Board Game Region Flood Fill
tasks.prompt:
A puzzle game board is a 6x6 grid of coloured regions. Each cell has a colour id from 1 to 4:

Row 0: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3
Row 1: 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3
Row 2: 4, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3
Row 3: 4, 4, 1, 2, 2, 3
Row 4: 4, 4, 4, 4, 2, 3
Row 5: 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3

The player selects the cell at row 2, column 2. The connected region containing that cell consists of all orthogonally adjacent cells sharing the same colour id (no diagonals).

Output exactly these lines:
Selected colour: C
Region size: S
Region bounding box: top T, left L, bottom B, right R

where C is the colour id of the selected cell, S is the number of cells in the region, and T, L, B, R are the minimum row, minimum column, maximum row, maximum column of the region cells (0-indexed).
tasks.expected_stdout:
Selected colour: 1
Region size: 8
Region bounding box: top 0, left 0, bottom 3, right 2
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Community Garden Plot Rotation
tasks.prompt:
A community garden has a 5x5 grid of plots. Each plot grows a crop represented by a single letter: T for tomatoes, B for beans, C for corn, K for kale. The current layout is:

Row 0: T, T, B, C, K
Row 1: T, B, B, C, K
Row 2: T, T, B, C, K
Row 3: T, B, B, C, K
Row 4: T, T, B, C, K

The gardeners rotate crops one column to the right each season: the crop in column 4 wraps around to column 0. Rows stay fixed.

After ONE rotation, output exactly these lines:
Row 0: <5 letters separated by single spaces>
Row 1: <5 letters separated by single spaces>
Row 2: <5 letters separated by single spaces>
Row 3: <5 letters separated by single spaces>
Row 4: <5 letters separated by single spaces>

then a blank line is NOT printed; immediately followed by:
Column counts: T=a B=b C=c K=k

where a, b, c, k are the total counts of each crop across the entire rotated grid.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Row 0: K T T B C
Row 1: K T B B C
Row 2: K T T B C
Row 3: K T B B C
Row 4: K T T B C
Column counts: T=8 B=7 C=5 K=5
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Aquarium Fish Territory Map
tasks.prompt:
An aquarium has a 6x6 grid of territories. Each territory is claimed by one of three fish: fish A, fish B, or fish C (represented as A, B, C). The map is:

Row 0: A, A, A, B, B, B
Row 1: A, A, A, B, B, B
Row 2: A, A, C, C, B, B
Row 3: C, C, C, C, B, B
Row 4: C, C, C, B, B, B
Row 5: C, C, C, B, B, B

Fish A expands one cell per round: after each round, any cell orthogonally adjacent (up, down, left, right) to an A cell that is currently not A becomes A. This expansion happens simultaneously for all A cells in the round.

Run exactly 2 expansion rounds.

Output exactly these lines:
Round 1 A cells: R1
Round 2 A cells: R2
Final A share: P.P%

where R1 and R2 are the total count of A cells after round 1 and after round 2 respectively, and P.P is the final percentage of A cells out of 36 total cells, rounded to 1 decimal place.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Round 1 A cells: 13
Round 2 A cells: 19
Final A share: 52.8%
tasks.category: grid simulations on a small fixed 2-D grid (cellular rules, paths, regions, scoring)

tasks.title: Museum Artifact Authenticity Check
tasks.prompt:
A museum curator is verifying the authenticity of a set of small bronze tokens using a number-theory test. Each token has a catalog number. A token is considered "verified" if the sum of its digits is divisible by the number of digits in the catalog number, and the catalog number itself is divisible by 7.

The catalog numbers to check are: 3472, 819, 5555, 1001, 9999, 210, 4096.

For each token, output a line in the format:
TOKEN <number>: VERIFIED
or
TOKEN <number>: REJECTED

After processing all tokens, output a final line:
TOTAL VERIFIED: <count>

Output exactly 8 lines total, in the order the numbers are given. No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
TOKEN 3472: VERIFIED
TOKEN 819: VERIFIED
TOKEN 5555: REJECTED
TOKEN 1001: REJECTED
TOKEN 9999: REJECTED
TOKEN 210: VERIFIED
TOKEN 4096: REJECTED
TOTAL VERIFIED: 3
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.title: Weather Station Barometer Base Conversion
tasks.prompt:
A weather station records barometer readings as integers and must convert them to base 6 for its archive system. A reading is "stable" if it is divisible by 6.

The readings (in decimal) are: 215, 42, 100, 36, 77, 12.

For each reading, output a line:
DEC <decimal> -> BASE6 <digits>
where <digits> is the base-6 representation (digits 0-5, no prefix).

After all readings, output:
STABLE COUNT: <number of readings divisible by 6>

Output exactly 7 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
DEC 215 -> BASE6 555
DEC 42 -> BASE6 110
DEC 100 -> BASE6 244
DEC 36 -> BASE6 100
DEC 77 -> BASE6 205
DEC 12 -> BASE6 20
STABLE COUNT: 3
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.prompt:
A ferry service issues 6-digit ticket codes. A code is "balanced" if the sum of the first three digits equals the sum of the last three digits.

The ticket codes are: 123321, 456654, 111000, 987123, 555555, 246810.

For each ticket, output:
TICKET <code>: BALANCED
or
TICKET <code>: UNBALANCED

Then output a final line:
BALANCED TOTAL: <count>

Output exactly 7 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
TICKET 123321: BALANCED
TICKET 456654: BALANCED
TICKET 111000: UNBALANCED
TICKET 987123: UNBALANCED
TICKET 555555: BALANCED
TICKET 246810: UNBALANCED
BALANCED TOTAL: 3
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.prompt:
A train network assigns route IDs. For each route ID, compute the product of its digits. If the product is even, the route is "EXPRESS"; otherwise it is "LOCAL".

The route IDs are: 357, 246, 111, 804, 999, 500.

For each route output:
ROUTE <id>: PRODUCT <product> EXPRESS
or
ROUTE <id>: PRODUCT <product> LOCAL

Then output:
EXPRESS COUNT: <count>

Output exactly 7 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
ROUTE 357: PRODUCT 105 LOCAL
ROUTE 246: PRODUCT 48 EXPRESS
ROUTE 111: PRODUCT 1 LOCAL
ROUTE 804: PRODUCT 0 EXPRESS
ROUTE 999: PRODUCT 729 LOCAL
ROUTE 500: PRODUCT 0 EXPRESS
EXPRESS COUNT: 3
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

A harbor crane operator must check container weights. A container is "clear to lift" if its weight in kilograms is divisible by both 12 and 8. Otherwise it needs a "SECOND CHECK".

For each container output:
CONTAINER <weight>kg: CLEAR
or
CONTAINER <weight>kg: SECOND CHECK

Then output:
CLEARED: <count> / 7

Output exactly 8 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
CONTAINER 96kg: CLEAR
CONTAINER 144kg: CLEAR
CONTAINER 50kg: SECOND CHECK
CONTAINER 240kg: CLEAR
CONTAINER 72kg: CLEAR
CONTAINER 100kg: SECOND CHECK
CONTAINER 48kg: CLEAR
CLEARED: 5 / 7

STAR <id>: NOTABLE

STAR <id>: ORDINARY

NOTABLE COUNT: <count>

tasks.title: Aquarium Pump Cycle Remainder
tasks.prompt:
An aquarium's pump controller cycles through 11 speeds. Given a target speed and a starting offset, the effective speed is (target + offset) mod 11. If the effective speed is 0, the pump is OFF.

The pairs (target, offset) are:
(7, 4), (10, 3), (0, 0), (5, 7), (9, 2), (3, 9).

For each pair output:
TARGET <target> OFFSET <offset> -> SPEED <effective>
or
TARGET <target> OFFSET <offset> -> PUMP OFF

Then output:
OFF COUNT: <count>

Output exactly 7 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
TARGET 7 OFFSET 4 -> PUMP OFF
TARGET 10 OFFSET 3 -> SPEED 2
TARGET 0 OFFSET 0 -> PUMP OFF
TARGET 5 OFFSET 7 -> SPEED 1
TARGET 9 OFFSET 2 -> PUMP OFF
TARGET 3 OFFSET 9 -> SPEED 1
OFF COUNT: 3
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.title: Cinema Ticket Digit Reverse Check
tasks.prompt:
A cinema issues 4-digit ticket numbers. A ticket is a "mirror" if reversing its digits yields the same number (i.e., it reads the same forwards and backwards).

The ticket numbers are: 1221, 3456, 7887, 1001, 5432, 9999.

For each ticket output:
TICKET <number>: MIRROR
or
TICKET <number>: NOT MIRROR

Then output:
MIRROR COUNT: <count>

Output exactly 7 lines, in the order given. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
TICKET 1221: MIRROR
TICKET 3456: NOT MIRROR
TICKET 7887: MIRROR
TICKET 1001: MIRROR
TICKET 5432: NOT MIRROR
TICKET 9999: MIRROR
MIRROR COUNT: 4
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.title: Ferry Manifest Vowel Check
tasks.prompt:
You are processing a manifest of passenger cabin codes for a ferry. Each code consists of exactly 3 uppercase letters followed by a space and a 2-digit number.

Write a program that processes the following list of cabin codes:
["A12 B7", "C4 D9", "E6 F3"]

For each code, count how many vowels (A, E, I, O, U) appear in the 3-letter portion. A code is considered "lucky" if it contains at least 2 vowels.

Output exactly 6 lines. The first 3 lines correspond to the 3 codes in order. Each line must be formatted as:
Code: [original code] | Vowels: [count] | Status: [lucky/ok]

The last 3 lines summarize the results:
Lucky Codes: [count of lucky codes]
Total Vowels: [total vowels across all codes]
Longest Code: [the code with the most vowels, if tied pick the first one]

No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Code: A12 B7 | Vowels: 1 | Status: ok
Code: C4 D9 | Vowels: 0 | Status: ok
Code: E6 F3 | Vowels: 1 | Status: ok
Lucky Codes: 0
Total Vowels: 2
Longest Code: A12 B7
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Train Schedule Digit Swap
tasks.prompt:
You are working at a train station. A train's departure time is given as a 4-digit text string in HHMM format (e.g. "0930"). Due to a system glitch, the first two digits (hours) and the last two digits (minutes) have been swapped for some trains.

Given the list of glitched times:
["1245", "0830", "2315", "0705"]

For each time string:
1. Swap the first two characters with the last two characters to get the correct time.
2. Check if the corrected time is valid (hours 00-23, minutes 00-59).
3. Output the corrected time as HH:MM.

Output exactly 5 lines:
Line 1: [corrected time 1] [valid/invalid]
Line 2: [corrected time 2] [valid/invalid]
Line 3: [corrected time 3] [valid/invalid]
Line 4: [corrected time 4] [valid/invalid]
Line 5: Valid Count: [number of valid times]

No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
45:12 invalid
30:08 invalid
15:23 valid
05:07 valid
Valid Count: 2
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Playlist Tag Frequency
tasks.prompt:

["pop", "rock", "jazz", "pop", "jazz", "pop", "rock", "pop"]

Line 1: pop: [count]
Line 2: rock: [count]
Line 3: jazz: [count]
Line 4: Total Songs: [total]
Line 5: Most Popular: [tag]

pop: 4
rock: 2
jazz: 2
Total Songs: 8
Most Popular: pop

tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.prompt:
A vending machine has slots labeled with codes like "A1", "B3", "C2". The first character is a letter A-C and the second is a digit 1-4.

The following slots are currently occupied:
["A1", "B3", "C2", "A5", "D1", "B3"]

Slot [index+1]: [code] -> [VALID/INVALID]

Line 7: Unique Valid Slots: [count]

Slot 2: B3 -> VALID
Slot 3: C2 -> VALID
Slot 4: A5 -> INVALID
Slot 5: D1 -> INVALID
Slot 6: B3 -> VALID
Unique Valid Slots: 3
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.prompt:

Line 1: [ID 1] [EVEN/ODD]
Line 2: [ID 2] [EVEN/ODD]
Line 3: [ID 3] [EVEN/ODD]
Line 4: [ID 4] [EVEN/ODD]
Line 5: Even Sum Count: [count of IDs where sum is even]

No trailing spaces.

WXYZ-1234 EVEN
QRST-5678 EVEN
ABCD-9012 EVEN
MNOP-3456 EVEN
Even Sum Count: 4
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Cinema Seat Row Formatter
tasks.prompt:
A cinema assigns seats as text strings like "A1", "A2", "B5". The first character is the row letter (A-Z) and the rest is the seat number.

The following seats are booked:
["A1", "A2", "B1", "C10", "A1", "B2"]

1. Determine the row letter.
2. Count how many seats in that row are booked so far (including this one).
3. Output the booking as: Row [letter] Seat [number] ([count] in row)

If a seat appears twice, it is counted once for uniqueness but both bookings are printed.

Output exactly 7 lines:
Lines 1-6: The formatted booking lines as described above.
Line 7: Rows Used: [number of distinct rows used]

No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Row A Seat 1 (1 in row)
Row A Seat 2 (2 in row)
Row B Seat 1 (1 in row)
Row C Seat 10 (1 in row)
Row A Seat 1 (3 in row)
Row B Seat 2 (2 in row)
Rows Used: 3
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Hotel Key Card Validation
tasks.prompt:
Hotel key cards have IDs formatted as 2 uppercase letters, a hyphen, and 3 digits (e.g. "AB-123").

The following key cards are issued:
["AB-123", "CD-456", "EF-789", "GH-012", "AB-123", "IJ-345"]

For each card:
1. Check if it is a duplicate of an earlier card in the list.

A vending machine's stock file uses key=value lines. Each line has the form `slot=<Int>;item=<Text>;qty=<Int>;price=<Real>` where `price` is in dollars with exactly 2 decimal places.

The input is:
```
slot=1;item=COLA;qty=12;price=1.75
slot=2;item=CHIPS;qty=8;price=2.25
slot=3;item=COLA;qty=5;price=1.75
slot=4;item=CANDY;qty=15;price=1.25
slot=5;item=CHIPS;qty=3;price=2.25
slot=6;item=WATER;qty=20;price=1.00
```

Compute the total value (qty * price) of stock for each distinct item name, then print items in alphabetical order. Print each item's total value with exactly 2 decimal places.

Output format (one line per item, alphabetical by item name, no trailing spaces):
```
CANDY: 18.75
CHIPS: 24.75
COLA: 30.63
WATER: 20.00
```

Note: 5 * 1.75 + 12 * 1.75 = 30.625, which rounds to 30.63 with 2 decimal places.
tasks.expected_stdout:
CANDY: 18.75
CHIPS: 24.75
COLA: 29.75
WATER: 20.00
tasks.category: parsing simple line-based text formats given inline (key=value lines, commands, fixed-width fields)

tasks.title: School Locker Command Tally
tasks.prompt:
A school issues locker commands in the format `OPEN <locker>` or `CLOSE <locker>` where `<locker>` is an Int from 1 to 8.

The input commands, in order, are:
```
OPEN 3
OPEN 7
OPEN 1
CLOSE 7
OPEN 5
CLOSE 1
OPEN 3
CLOSE 5
```

Process each command: OPEN sets that locker to open (Bool true), CLOSE sets it to closed (Bool false). After all commands, count how many lockers are open out of lockers 1 through 8, and list which ones are open in ascending order.

Output format (exactly two lines, no trailing spaces):
```
Open count: 1
Open lockers: 3
```

(If more than one locker were open, the second line would list them separated by single spaces, e.g. `Open lockers: 3 5 7`.)
tasks.expected_stdout:
Open count: 1
Open lockers: 3
tasks.category: parsing simple line-based text formats given inline (key=value lines, commands, fixed-width fields)

tasks.title: Ferry Fare Fixed-Width Ticket Parser
tasks.prompt:
A ferry ticket printer uses fixed-width fields. Each ticket line has exactly 14 characters: positions 1-3 are the passenger count (Int, right-aligned or left-aligned within 3 chars), position 4 is a space, positions 5-6 are the fare class Text (AD for adult, CH for child), position 7 is a space, and positions 8-14 are the fare in cents as an Int (7 digits).

The input ticket lines are:
```
  2 AD    1550
  1 CH     700
  3 AD    2325
  4 CH    2800
  1 AD     775
```

Parse each line. For each ticket, compute the fare per person in cents (fare / passengers). Print one line per ticket as `class passengers farePerPerson` where farePerPerson is an Int (integer division, truncated). Print tickets in the order given.

Output format (exactly five lines, no trailing spaces):
```
AD 2 775
CH 1 700
AD 3 775
CH 4 700
AD 1 775
```
tasks.category: parsing simple line-based text formats given inline (key=value lines, commands, fixed-width fields)

tasks.title: Garden Harvest Key-Value Summary
tasks.prompt:
A community garden logs harvests using key=value lines. Each line has the form `plot=<Int>;crop=<Text>;kg=<Real>` where kg has exactly 1 decimal place.

The input is:
```
plot=1;crop=TOMATO;kg=12.5
plot=2;crop=LETTUCE;kg=4.3
plot=3;crop=TOMATO;kg=8.7
plot=4;crop=CARROT;kg=6.1
plot=5;crop=LETTUCE;kg=5.9
plot=6;crop=TOMATO;kg=10.2
```

Sum the kg for each crop, then print the crop with the highest total first, then the others in descending order of total. Print each total with exactly 1 decimal place.

Output format (one line per crop, no trailing spaces):
```
TOMATO 31.4
CARROT 6.1
LETTUCE 10.2
```

Wait — order must be strictly descending by total: TOMATO 31.4, then LETTUCE 10.2, then CARROT 6.1. Correct output:
```
TOMATO 31.4
LETTUCE 10.2
CARROT 6.1
```

TOMATO 31.4
LETTUCE 10.2
CARROT 6.1

tasks.title: Laundromat Dryer Slot Scheduler
tasks.prompt:
Write a program that schedules dryer usage at a laundromat. The laundromat has 3 dryers (D1, D2, D3). Each dryer can hold one load at a time.

There are 6 loads waiting. Each load has an ID and a required drying time in minutes. The loads arrive in the order listed below. When a load arrives, if a dryer is free it starts immediately; otherwise the load waits until the earliest dryer becomes free. If multiple dryers become free at the same time, use the lowest-numbered dryer.

Loads (in arrival order):
1. L1, 40 minutes
2. L2, 30 minutes
3. L3, 25 minutes
4. L4, 35 minutes
5. L5, 20 minutes
6. L6, 45 minutes

All loads arrive at time 0.

For each load in arrival order, print the dryer it is assigned to and the time (in minutes from 0) at which it finishes.

Output format — one line per load, exactly as shown (no extra spaces):
L1 D1 40
L2 D2 30
L3 D3 25
L4 D1 75
L5 D2 50
L6 D3 70

Note: The example above shows the format only — you must compute the actual finish times based on the algorithm described (greedy assignment to earliest-available dryer, ties broken by lowest dryer number).

tasks.title: Emergency Room Triage Queue
tasks.prompt:
An emergency room processes patients using a simple priority queue. Each patient has an ID, a severity score (1–5, higher = more urgent), and an arrival time (minutes from opening).

Patients (in arrival order):
1. P1, severity 3, arrives at 0
2. P2, severity 5, arrives at 2
3. P3, severity 1, arrives at 4
4. P4, severity 4, arrives at 5
5. P5, severity 2, arrives at 7

Processing rules:
- There is one doctor. The doctor picks the waiting patient with the highest severity; ties broken by earliest arrival time.
- Each patient takes exactly 10 minutes to treat.
- A patient who arrives while the doctor is busy waits.
- A newly arrived patient with higher severity than the one currently being treated does NOT interrupt; the current treatment finishes first.
- The doctor starts at time 0 with an empty queue; if no one is waiting, the doctor idles until the next arrival.

Print one line per patient in the order they are TREATED:
Px at TTT
where TTT is the time (minutes) treatment finishes.

Output exactly 5 lines, no trailing spaces.

P1 at 10
P2 at 20
P4 at 30
P5 at 40
P3 at 50

tasks.title: Robot Maze Shortest Path Patterns

Write a program that prints every valid path (as a string of R and D moves) that passes through exactly these 2 wet cells (it may pass through one wet cell more than once if revisiting, but note the robot never revisits cells on a monotonic path — so simply: paths that pass through both wet cells).

tasks.title: Library Return Slot State Machine
tasks.prompt:
A library return slot has three states: EMPTY, HOLDING, and OVERDUE. A sensor reports events as text codes:
- "IN" means a book was dropped in.
- "OUT" means the librarian removed the top book.
- "ACK" means the librarian acknowledged an overdue notice.

State rules:
- Start in EMPTY.
- EMPTY + IN -> HOLDING
- HOLDING + IN -> HOLDING (stack grows)
- HOLDING + OUT -> HOLDING if at least one book remains after removal, else EMPTY.
- HOLDING + OUT when the stack has been full (3 books) at some point -> OVERDUE.
- OVERDUE + ACK -> EMPTY (stack cleared).
- OVERDUE + IN -> OVERDUE.
- Any state + an event not listed above -> stay in current state.

The event sequence is:
"IN", "IN", "OUT", "IN", "IN", "OUT", "OUT", "ACK", "IN"

Track both the state and the stack size (number of books currently in the slot). The stack size starts at 0 and only changes on IN (size +1) and OUT (size -1, never below 0). The "full" flag becomes true whenever size reaches 3.

Print exactly the following lines (no trailing spaces):
Line 1: Final state: <state>
Line 2: Final stack size: <n>
Line 3: Reached full: <YES or NO>
Line 4: Event count: <total number of events processed>

Example of format (not the answer): Final state: HOLDING
tasks.expected_stdout:
Final state: HOLDING
Final stack size: 1
Reached full: YES
Event count: 9
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Lighthouse Beacon Rotation Controller
tasks.prompt:
A lighthouse beacon rotates and can be in one of three modes: OFF, SLOW, or FAST. A control panel sends a sequence of commands as text:
- "ON" turns the beacon on (mode becomes SLOW).
- "BOOST" increases speed: SLOW -> FAST.
- "DIM" decreases speed: FAST -> SLOW.
- "OFF" turns the beacon off (mode becomes OFF).
- "MAINT" triggers maintenance: any mode -> OFF.

Speed in rotations per minute: OFF = 0, SLOW = 6, FAST = 18.

The command sequence is:
"ON", "BOOST", "BOOST", "DIM", "ON", "MAINT", "ON", "BOOST", "OFF", "ON"

Commands not matching any rule leave the mode unchanged. "BOOST" in FAST stays FAST; "DIM" in SLOW stays SLOW; "ON" when already on keeps the current speed.

Print exactly:
Line 1: Final mode: <OFF or SLOW or FAST>
Line 2: Rotations per minute: <integer>
Line 3: Commands processed: <count>
Line 4: BOOST commands: <count of BOOST in sequence>
Line 5: Mode changes: <number of times the mode actually changed after a command>

tasks.title: Library Barcode Check Digit
tasks.prompt:
The library uses a 13-digit ISBN-like barcode where the check digit is computed as follows: take the first 12 digits, multiply digits in odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, ...) by 1 and even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th, ...) by 3, sum them, and the check digit is the value that makes the total sum divisible by 10.

You are given four books with their first 12 digits:
  Book A: 978 0 306 40615 7 -> digits: 9,7,8,0,3,0,6,4,0,6,1,5
  Book B: 978 1 861 00230 1 -> digits: 9,7,8,1,8,6,1,0,0,2,3,0
  Book C: 978 0 134 09079 7 -> digits: 9,7,8,0,1,3,4,0,9,0,7,9
  Book D: 978 0 471 15072 5 -> digits: 9,7,8,0,4,7,1,1,5,0,7,2

For each book, compute the weighted sum of the 12 digits (odd positions x1, even positions x3), then compute the check digit needed to make the total divisible by 10, and finally output the full 13-digit barcode as a single number.

Output format (exactly 4 lines, no trailing spaces):
  Barcode A: <13-digit number>
  Barcode B: <13-digit number>
  Barcode C: <13-digit number>
  Barcode D: <13-digit number>

Each <13-digit number> is the 12 given digits followed by the computed check digit, printed as one continuous integer with no spaces.

tasks.title: Orchard Harvest Crate Label Audit
tasks.prompt:
An orchard packs apples in wooden crates. Each crate lid carries a printed label of the form "OR-<digits>-<letter>" where <digits> is 3 digits and <letter> is a single uppercase letter A through E. Here are the labels as they came off the packing line, in order:

"OR-104-B"
"OR-221-F"
"OR-330-A"
"OR-417-D"
"OR-509-C"
"OR-612-E"
"OR-735-B"
"OR-841-Z"
"OR-928-A"

A label is valid if and only if it has exactly the shape described above: the prefix "OR-", exactly three characters that are all digits '0'..'9', a '-', and exactly one character in 'A'..'E'. Write a program that prints a report.

Output format (exactly these lines, no trailing spaces):

VALID COUNT: <n>
INVALID COUNT: <n>
VALID SUM: <s>
VALID MEAN: <m>

where <n> are integer counts, <s> is the sum of the 3-digit numbers appearing in the valid labels (integer), and <m> is that sum divided by the valid count, printed with exactly 1 decimal place.
tasks.expected_stdout:
VALID COUNT: 7
INVALID COUNT: 2
VALID SUM: 3635
VALID MEAN: 519.3
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Garden Seed Packet Code Check
tasks.prompt:
A community garden stores seed packets, each stamped with a code of the form "<uppercase letter><2 digits><uppercase letter>". The 8 codes are:

"T14R"
"B27K"
"L09M"
"P41S"
"R33T"
"G52N"
"H68P"
"Q7Q"

A code is well formed if and only if it is exactly 4 characters long: character 1 is an uppercase letter 'A'..'Z', characters 2 and 3 are digits '0'..'9', character 4 is an uppercase letter 'A'..'Z'. Write a program that prints a report.

Output format (exactly these lines, no trailing spaces):

TOTAL: <t>
WELL FORMED: <w>
MALFORMED: <m>
DIGIT SUM: <d>

where <t> is the total number of codes, <w> the number of well-formed codes, <m> the number of malformed codes, and <d> is the sum over ALL codes of every digit character they contain (each digit character counts its numeric value; a malformed code still contributes any digits it happens to contain), printed as an integer.
tasks.expected_stdout:
TOTAL: 8
WELL FORMED: 7
MALFORMED: 1
DIGIT SUM: 62
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Fitness Log Heart Rate Zone Tally
tasks.prompt:
A fitness log records heart-rate readings as text strings, each of the form "<3 digits> bpm" or "<3 digits>bpm" (with or without the space). Readings that do not have exactly 3 digits followed by an optional single space and then "bpm" are marked "BAD". Here are the 10 readings in order:

"142 bpm"
"98 bpm"
"167bpm"
"120 bpm"
"75 bpm"
"183 bpm"
"201 bpm"
"12 bpm"
"156 bpm"
"BAD"

Write a program that prints a report.

Output format (exactly these lines, no trailing spaces):

GOOD: <g>
BAD: <b>
MAX GOOD: <mx>
MIN GOOD: <mn>
AVG GOOD: <a>

where <g> and <b> are counts, <mx> and <mn> are the maximum and minimum numeric values among the GOOD readings (integers, printed with no leading zeros), and <a> is the average of the GOOD readings printed with exactly 1 decimal place. (The literal string "BAD" counts toward <b>.)
tasks.expected_stdout:
GOOD: 6
BAD: 4
MAX GOOD: 201
MIN GOOD: 120
AVG GOOD: 161.5
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Beekeeper Hive Frame Tag Sorter
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper labels hive frames with tags of the form "H<digit><letter>" where <digit> is one digit '0'..'9' and <letter> is an uppercase vowel 'A','E','I','O','U'. Here are the 9 tags in no particular order:

"H3A"
"H7O"
"H1I"
"H9U"
"H5E"
"H2O"
"H6A"
"H4I"
"H0X"

A tag is valid if and only if it is exactly 3 characters: 'H', one digit, then one uppercase vowel. Write a program that prints a report.

Output format (exactly these lines, no trailing spaces):

VALID TAGS: <list>
VALID COUNT: <c>
VOWEL COUNTS A E I O U: <a> <e> <i> <o> <u>

where <list> is the valid tags sorted lexicographically (ascending by character), separated by single spaces with no trailing space; <c> is the count of valid tags; and the vowel counts are the counts of each vowel among the third character of the valid tags, printed as five integers separated by single spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
VALID TAGS: H1I H2O H3A H4I H5E H6A H7O H9U
VALID COUNT: 8
VOWEL COUNTS A E I O U: 2 1 2 2 1
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Library Call Number Validator
tasks.prompt:
A small library validates call numbers written as text of the form "<2 uppercase letters>/<3 digits>". Here are the 8 call numbers as recorded:

"QC/101"
"QA/205"
"HB/330"
"QC/447"
"ZZ/512"
"Q/99"
"RT/604"
"MK/777"

A call number is valid if and only if it is exactly 7 characters: two uppercase letters, a '/', then three digits. Write a program that prints a report.

Output format (exactly these lines, no trailing spaces):

VALID: <v>
INVALID: <i>
PREFIX Q COUNT: <q>
FIRST VALID: <fv>
LAST VALID: <lv>

where <v> and <i> are counts; <q> is how many of the 8 call numbers start with the letter 'Q' (count regardless of validity); <fv> is the first valid call number in the original order; <lv> is the last valid call number in the original order; if there are no valid call numbers print NONE for those two fields.
tasks.expected_stdout:

INVALID: 1
PREFIX Q COUNT: 4
FIRST VALID: QC/101
LAST VALID: MK/777
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Parking Garage Entry Exit Log

RejectedEntries: <count>

Step 2: signal 1 -> OPENING
Step 3: signal 3 -> OPENING

Step 6: signal 1 -> CLOSING
Step 7: signal 3 -> OPENING

A bus stop display logs the route code of each bus that arrives in one hour. The route codes, in order, are:

["12", "7", "12", "3", "7", "12", "7", "3", "12", "7"]

Write a program that counts how many times each route code appears. Print one line per route code, sorted numerically by the route code (smallest number first).

Output format: one line per route code, exactly as shown, with no extra spaces:
3: 2
7: 4
12: 4

The output must be exactly 3 lines with no trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.category: counting and tallying by a text key over a fixed list (word frequencies, votes, item counts); the task states the output order: first appearance or sorted by key or by count with a tie rule

tasks.prompt:

  "East" 2.50
  "South" 6.00
  "East" 3.75

Group the sessions by zone. Print one line per zone, ordered alphabetically by zone name, in this exact format:

  <ZoneName> sessions=<count> total=$<total> avg=$<average>

where <count> is the number of sessions for that zone, <total> is the sum of fees for that zone, and <average> is the mean fee for that zone. Print <total> and <average> as Real numbers with exactly 2 decimal places (e.g. 10.75). Each line has no trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
East sessions=3 total=$11.50 avg=$3.83
North sessions=3 total=$10.75 avg=$3.58
South sessions=3 total=$13.25 avg=$4.42

An aquarium has a 4x4 grid of coral fragments. Each cell records hours of light exposure per day. The grid rows are:
Row 1: 6, 8, 7, 5
Row 2: 9, 10, 8, 6
Row 3: 7, 9, 11, 7
Row 4: 5, 6, 7, 4

A fragment is HIGH if exposure >= 9, LOW if exposure <= 5, otherwise MEDIUM.

For each row, count how many fragments are HIGH, MEDIUM and LOW. Also report the fragment with the highest exposure (row and column, 1-indexed).

Print exactly the following five lines (no trailing spaces):
Row 1: high=0 medium=4 low=0
Row 2: high=2 medium=2 low=0
Row 3: high=2 medium=2 low=0
Row 4: high=0 medium=3 low=1
Highest exposure: row 3 column 3 value 11

Row 2: high=2 medium=2 low=0
Row 3: high=2 medium=2 low=0
Row 4: high=0 medium=2 low=2

tasks.title: Train Network Ticket Fare Modulo Check
tasks.prompt:
A regional train network sells tickets with fares that follow a hidden pattern. For each station name below, compute the ticket fare as follows: sum the positions (1-based) of all vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in the station name, multiply that sum by 7, then take the result modulo 9, and add 100.

Stations and their names (in this order):
1. RIVERSIDE
2. OAKHAVEN
3. BELLPORT
4. IRONGATE
5. SALTMEADOW

For each station, also determine whether the fare is even or odd.

Output exactly 10 lines: for each station, first a line with the station number, the station name, a space, the fare, then a second line with the station number and the word "even" or "odd" (lowercase), separated by a space. No trailing spaces.

Example format (for station 1 only):
1 RIVERSIDE 107
1 odd
tasks.expected_stdout:
1 RIVERSIDE 101
1 odd
2 OAKHAVEN 106
2 even
3 BELLPORT 102
3 even
4 IRONGATE 100
4 even
5 SALTMEADOW 106
5 even
tasks.category: number theory and integer arithmetic (divisors, digits, bases, modular patterns)

tasks.title: Weather Station Wind Code Validator
tasks.prompt:
A weather station records wind readings as short 4-character text codes. Each code has the format: one letter (N, S, E, or W) followed by three digits. The first digit must be 1, 2, or 3 (the speed group). The remaining two digits form a number from 00 to 99 (the bearing in tens of degrees).

Here are 8 recorded wind codes:
"N245", "S130", "E372", "W015", "N299", "E100", "S388", "W207"

A code is VALID if:
- The first character is one of N, S, E, W.
- The second character is 1, 2, or 3.
- All four characters are digits except the first.
- The bearing part (last two digits) is between 00 and 99.
- The speed digit and the tens digit of the bearing are not equal (e.g., N245 is invalid because the speed digit 2 equals the tens digit 4? No — invalid only if speed digit equals tens digit of bearing).

Wait, simplify: A code is VALID if the first character is N/S/E/W, the second character is 1, 2, or 3, and the speed digit (second character) is strictly greater than the tens digit of the bearing (third character). Otherwise it is INVALID.

Determine for each code whether it is VALID or INVALID.

Output exactly 8 lines, one per code, in the original order. Each line has the format:
CODE STATUS
where CODE is the original 4-character code and STATUS is either VALID or INVALID (uppercase, no other text). There is a single space between the code and the status. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
N245 INVALID
S130 INVALID
E372 INVALID
W015 INVALID
N299 INVALID
E100 VALID
S388 INVALID
W207 VALID
tasks.category: text processing on short fixed strings (counting, transforming, validating, formatting)

tasks.title: Recipe Book Spice Code Sum Checker

tasks.title: Weather Station City Code Distance
tasks.prompt:
A weather network uses 4-character city codes. The first two characters are uppercase letters (the region), and the last two are digits (the station number within the region).

Here are 8 city codes:
"NY12", "CA05", "TX33", "NY07", "FL21", "CA18", "TX09", "FL14"

But we want something different: compute the "station score" as the two-digit number times the letter value of the first character.

For each code, compute station_score = (letter_value_of_first_char) * (two_digit_number).

Then output the code and its station_score.

Output exactly 8 lines, one per code, in the original order:
<code> <station_score>

AVG_TAG 307.3

tasks.title: Beekeeper Apiary Feeding Round
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper makes a feeding round across an apiary. There are 5 hives, each needing syrup at a specific time (minutes after the start) and taking a certain number of minutes to fill:

Hive 1: needs syrup at minute 10, takes 4 minutes to fill
Hive 2: needs syrup at minute 12, takes 3 minutes to fill
Hive 3: needs syrup at minute 15, takes 6 minutes to fill
Hive 4: needs syrup at minute 20, takes 2 minutes to fill
Hive 5: needs syrup at minute 22, takes 5 minutes to fill

The beekeeper works through the hives in order of Hive number. When the beekeeper arrives at a hive, if the hive's needed time has already passed, the beekeeper feeds it immediately; otherwise the beekeeper waits until the needed time. The beekeeper then feeds the hive (which takes the stated minutes) before moving on. The beekeeper starts at minute 0 at Hive 1.

For each hive, print the minute the beekeeper finishes feeding it.

Output format (5 lines, one per hive):
Hive N finish: M
where N is the hive number (1-5) and M is the finish minute as an integer. There are no spaces other than shown. Print the lines in order Hive 1 through Hive 5.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Hive 1 finish: 14
Hive 2 finish: 17
Hive 3 finish: 23
Hive 4 finish: 25
Hive 5 finish: 30
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)
